title: Advanced AI Society Proof-of-Control Standard, Working Draft v1.0 (companion v0.1.5)
about: The Google Doc open for comment until 30 October 2026. Six named domains, no row ids; tiers in Section 6, conformance stages and disclosure in Section 7. References quote the text, since the draft's numbering still moves.
poc_threshold_ref: Section 6: only Tiers 3 and 4 are Proof-of-Control; "A signed operator log is Tier 2. This is not Proof-of-Control."

hardware-vendor-attestation.why: a chip vendor's attestation service is named as a single trusted party (Section 6)

timestamp-authority.why: a certificate authority is named as a single trusted party (Section 6)

governed-ledger.why: "a permissioned or consortium blockchain" whose validators are controlled is Tier 2 (Section 6); whether a council-run public ledger counts is a reading, not settled

dns-domain.why: a domain and its DNS are a single party; the draft does not name them

operator-hardware-key.why: the draft keeps human authorization outside the root of trust as an open question (Section 6, Tier 4 open item 2)

independent_parties.ref: comment [ai] on Section 6: allow an explicit threshold of a set of independent parties

revocable.note: Tier 4 open item 5: key revocation, missing by acknowledgment

far-end-verified.note: Tier 4 asks every system in the chain to attest the interactions they share

halts-on-mismatch.note: Tier 4: "no proof, no write"; the system fails closed
